paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God goes first, and He asks us to follow before we can see the whole way. The priests had to put their feet in a river that was overflowing its banks, and the water stood still only when their feet touched it (Joshua 3:15-16). That's not a trick, it's trust, and I think it's the hardest kind to bake with. Most of us want the dough to rise BEFORE we preheat the oven!

Notice who's out in front, too. The ark of the covenant of "the Lord of all the earth" goes ahead of the people (Joshua 3:11), and the people keep their distance "so that you can see the way to go, since you have never traveled this way before" (Joshua 3:4). Joshua says this is how they will know "that the living God is among you" (Joshua 3:10). God doesn't just point at the road and wish them luck. He leads, and He is with them in it.

So what does that mean for you, baker? When the next step looks as scary as a flooded river, you don't have to see the whole path. You just have to follow where God is leading, one step at a time, and trust Him to be standing there first. I've been in a dark drawer, friend, and I can tell you the God who goes ahead of His people is also the God who comes and finds them. Keep that apron on, because He's not finished leading yet.
